jobs.occupation: Hyldetoftegaard A/S is looking for experienced, motivated and reliable seasonal workers EU/EEA citizens to join our team for the berry harvest season 2027 in Denmark.
jobs.description:
Hyldetoftegaard A/S is looking for experienced, motivated and reliable seasonal fruit pickers from EUROPE only EU/EEA countries to join our team for the 2027 berry harvest season in Denmark.

At our farm, we grow strawberries, raspberries and blackberries

During the summer season, we employ approximately 200–220 workers.

Working period:

The season runs from early May to end of October, depending on the harvest.

We offer you a working contract for the period of more than 16 weeks.

·        We recruit on an ongoing basis, with start dates beginning in early May.

·        New employees start each week, with the final employees starting at the end of June.

·        We prefer candidates who are willing to work until the end of the season in October.

Experience:

We are looking for experienced fruit pickers. Previous experience with fruit picking or agricultural work is important.

Applications without information about previous experience will not be considered.

Your job:

·        Picking strawberries, raspberries and blackberries in greenhouses and tunnels.

·        The work is physically demanding and requires a good level of fitness.

·        You must be prepared to work outdoors and in different weather conditions.

 **********************************************************************************************************

 

RECRUITMENT DAYS – CRAIOVA, ROMANIA – JANUARY 2027

 

RAMADA PLAZA CRAIOVA, Craiova, Romania

Recruitment dates:

 

·        Tuesday, 26 January 2027

·        Wednesday, 27 January 2027

 

Selected candidates will be invited to attend a short information meeting followed by individual employment interviews.

 

IMPORTANT – INVITATION ONLY

 

Attendance is strictly by individual invitation from Hyldetoftegaard A/S.

Only pre-selected candidates with a confirmed invitation will be admitted.

Unannounced visits and attendance without an invitation will be refused.

Applying does not guarantee an interview or an invitation.

***************************************************************************************************************

 Working conditions:

·        Work starts at 05:00 or 06:00.

·        6–7 working hours per day.

·        6 working days per week, with one changing day off.

·        Physically demanding work outdoors and in greenhouses in different weather conditions.

What to bring:

Please remember to bring:

-         Sleeping bag – Towels and other personal necessities

-         Warm clothing

-         Practical work clothes

-         Boots and waterproof clothing

-         Even in good weather, plants can be very wet in the morning.

Payment and Compensation

·        Payment is based on piecework and/or hourly wages throughout the season, depending on the quantity and quality of your work.

·        You will be registered with the Danish Tax Agency (SKAT).

·        Your salary will be transferred directly to your IBAN bank account, and you will receive an official pay slip.

Holiday Allowance:

Will be paid to “FerieKonto” and you will get them according to Danish holidays rules, when you apply for them after the working period. This also applies to foreign employees who work in Denmark and are covered by Danish holiday rules. You generally earn 12.5% of your salary as holiday pay.

Requirements:

·        EU/EEA citizenship and a valid passport or ID.

·        Good physical condition.

·        Previous fruit-picking or farm experience.

·        Ability to follow Danish safety and hygiene rules.

·        Ability to understand a little English

Accommodation:

 Accommodation (indoor) is available on or near the farm. 

Reasonable rent D. kr. 70,00 pr. day will be deducted from your wages.

Shared kitchen with facilities, bathroom and laundry facilities, internet electricity, water, heating, internet, and cleaning products for the maintenance of the accommodation provided.

Tax and health card:

The company applies for your tax card and health insurance card in accordance with the employment contract. These are valid for the agreed employment period. If you are married, you must provide documentation of your marital status.

Tax Deductions for Foreign Employees

Foreign employees working temporarily in Denmark may, depending on their individual tax situation, be entitled to certain tax deductions.

Travel deduction between the home country and Denmark
If you maintain your permanent home in your home country and your personal and financial interests remain there, you may be entitled to a tax deduction for transportation between your home country and your Danish workplace. This depends on your tax status in Denmark, and you must be able to document your journeys, for example by keeping tickets, receipts or other relevant documentation, around DKK 6.000 in 2026

Double housekeeping deduction
If your employment in Denmark is temporary and you maintain a home both in Denmark and in your home country, you may, under certain conditions, be entitled to a deduction for double housekeeping. This is intended for employees who have additional household expenses because their work requires them to live away from their permanent home.

To qualify, the employment must generally be temporary, and the distance between the two homes must be such that daily travel would not be reasonable. The deduction may be available for a maximum of two years.

For 2026, the standard deduction for double housekeeping is DKK 400 per week without documentation. A higher deduction may be possible if the actual expenses can be documented. The total deduction for food, accommodation and double housekeeping is subject to an annual maximum of DKK 34,400 in 2026.

Important: These deductions are not automatically granted. Each employee is responsible for checking whether they meet the conditions and for entering the relevant deductions on their Danish tax assessment. Documentation must be retained in case the Danish Tax Agency (Skattestyrelsen) requests it.

Transport to Denmark

You must arrange and pay for your own transport to Denmark.

Please bring your own car if possible. Having a car will make your stay much easier and more convenient, as you may need to travel between different farm locations and your accommodation in the nearby houses. It will also give you more freedom to get around and enjoy your time in the area.

HOW TO APPLY

If you wish to apply, send an email to job@hyldetoftegaard.dk and you will receive an application form.

See more: www.hyldetoftegaard.dk

Applicants wishing to attend an employment interview in Craiova must submit their completed application form and a copy of their ID card in advance.

You will then receive a separate invitation, which must be brought to the interview together with documentation of your previous work experience, as outlined in the instructions.

Important – Application Feedback

Only qualified applicants will be contacted.

If you do not receive a response from the company within 14 days of submitting your application, please consider that your application has not been successful and that you have not been selected to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

Thank you for your interest and understanding.

jobs.occupation: Experienced farm team leaders for the harvest 2027
jobs.description:
Hyldetoftegaard A/S is looking for several experienced, reliable and motivated Farm Team Leaders to join our team for the 2027 fruit harvest season in Denmark, we employ approximately 200–220 employees.

We are looking for people with practical experience in agriculture, horticulture or fruit production who can lead and organize teams of fruit pickers and make sure that the daily work is well planned and carried out efficiently.

RECRUITMENT DAYS – CRAIOVA, ROMANIA – JANUARY 2027

RAMADA PLAZA CRAIOVA, Craiova, Romania

Recruitment dates:

·        Tuesday, 26 January 2027

·        Wednesday, 27 January 2027

Selected candidates will be invited to attend a short information meeting followed by individual employment interviews.

IMPORTANT – INVITATION ONLY

Attendance is strictly by individual invitation from Hyldetoftegaard A/S.

Only pre-selected candidates with a confirmed invitation will be admitted.

Unannounced visits and attendance without an invitation will be refused.

Applying does not guarantee an interview or an invitation.

English is the working language within the company.

YOUR MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

·        Lead and organize a team of fruit pickers.

·        Plan and distribute the daily work among the workers.

·        Give clear instructions and make sure that tasks are understood.

·        Follow up on the team's daily work, progress and productivity.

·        Make sure that fruit picking is carried out efficiently and correctly.

·        Support the team and solve practical problems during the working day.

·        Register and report the team's daily harvest and output.

·        Keep simple and accurate records of workers, working hours and daily production.

·        Communicate daily information clearly to farm management.

·        Help ensure that safety, hygiene and company rules are followed.

ADMINISTRATIVE RESPONSIBILITIES

The Team Leaders will also have simple administrative responsibilities. You must be comfortable recording daily information and reporting it to management.

·        Register the team's daily fruit harvest/output.

·        Keep track of daily work and working hours.

·        Prepare simple daily reports.

·        Report relevant information and issues to farm management.

ENGLISH – REQUIRED

You must be able to communicate in English with management, understand information and handle everyday communication.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

·        Previous experience as a team leader, supervisor, foreman or similar position.

·        Experience from agriculture, horticulture, fruit production or another relevant field.

·        Experience leading, motivating and organizing a team of workers.

·        Good communication and organizational skills.

·        Ability to take responsibility and work independently.

·        A positive and respectful approach to working with people from different countries.

·        Good English communication skills – required.

·        Good physical condition and willingness to work alongside the team when necessary.

WORKING PERIOD

The 2027 fruit harvest season runs from early May to mid-September or the end of October, depending on the harvest, we prefer you start in February and until Mid – end of October

The exact employment period will be agreed according to the farm's needs and your availability.

WORKING HOURS

·        Work normally starts at 05:00 or 06:00.

·        Approximately 6–7 working hours per day.

·        6 working days per week, with one changing day off.

·        Flexibility is required during busy periods of the harvest.

SALARY

Farm Team Leaders are employed on a fixed monthly salary.

The starting salary is a minimum of DKK 24.000.

The salary will be agreed according to qualifications, previous experience and the responsibilities of the position.

IBAN bank account:

You can only register one IBAN bank account in your own name for salary payments during your employment period.

ACCOMMODATION

Indoor accommodation is available on or near the farm, for the day’s price. Dkr.70,00 will be deducted from salary.

Shared kitchen, bathroom and laundry facilities. The company provides free access to a washing machine, tumble dryer, electricity, water, heating, internet, and cleaning products for the maintenance of the accommodation provided.

 TAX CARD AND HEALTH INSURANCE CARD

The company will apply for your tax card and health insurance card in accordance with your employment contract. These cards will be valid for the agreed employment period. If you are married, you must provide documentation of your marital status.

TAX DEDUCTIONS FOR FOREIGN EMPLOYEES

Foreign employees working temporarily in Denmark may be eligible for certain tax deductions, depending on their individual tax situation.

 Travel between your home country and Denmark

If you maintain your permanent home in your home country and your personal and financial ties remain there, you may be eligible for a deduction for travel between your home country and your workplace in Denmark. Eligibility depends on your Danish tax status. You must keep documentation of your journeys, such as tickets and receipts. The amount shown for 2026 is approximately DKK 6,000.

Double-household deduction

If your employment in Denmark is temporary and you maintain a home both in Denmark and in your home country, you may, under certain conditions, qualify for a deduction for additional household expenses. This may apply when your work requires you to live away from your permanent home.

To qualify, your employment must generally be temporary, and the distance between the two homes must make daily travel unreasonable. The deduction may be available for up to two years.

For 2026, the standard deduction for double housekeeping is DKK 400 per week without documentation. A higher deduction may be possible if you can document your actual expenses. The total deduction for food, accommodation and double housekeeping is subject to an annual maximum of DKK 34,400 for 2026. 

Important: These deductions are not automatic. You are responsible for checking whether you qualify and for entering the relevant deductions on your Danish tax assessment. Keep your documentation in case the Danish Tax Agency requests it.

TRANSPORT TO DENMARK

You must arrange and pay for your own transport to Denmark.

 If possible, bring your own car. A car can make your stay easier and more convenient, as you may need to travel between different farm locations and your accommodation in nearby houses. It will also give you more freedom to explore the local area.

TRACTOR DRIVING & FORKLIFT CERTIFICATE – ADVANTAGES, NOT REQUIREMENTS

These qualifications are wishes from the company and will be considered positively. However, our main priority is to employ good Team Leaders who can lead people, organize the daily work and take responsibility.

HOW TO APPLY:

If you wish to apply, send an email to job@hyldetoftegaard.dk and you will receive an application form. See more at www.hyldetoftegaard.dk

Applicants wishing to attend an employment interview in Craiova must submit their completed application form and a copy of their ID card in advance.

You will then receive a separate invitation, which must be brought to the interview together with documentation of your previous work experience, as outlined in the instructions

 Important – Application Feedback

Only qualified applicants will be contacted.

If you do not receive a response from the company within 14 days of submitting your application, please consider that your application has not been successful and that you have not been selected to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

Thank you for your interest and understanding.

Restaurant Okê | Ruths Hotel | Skagen, Denmark

Join the team at Restaurant Okê.

We are looking for a talented and ambitious Sous Chef with a strong passion for pastry and desserts to join our Michelin-starred Restaurant Okê, located at Ruths Hotel in the heart of Gl. Skagen, Denmark.

At Okê, our cuisine is shaped by the seasons, exceptional ingredients and a dedication to craftsmanship. Four times a year, we introduce a new signature menu, allowing us to continuously explore new flavours, techniques and creative expressions.

As our Sous Chef specialising in pastry, you will play a key role in developing and executing the restaurant's desserts and sweet creations. Working closely with Executive Head Chef Jack Cramer and our dedicated kitchen team, you will have the opportunity to contribute your own ideas and help shape the future of Okê's pastry offering.

About you

• 
You have solid experience in fine dining, preferably within a Michelin-starred restaurant.

• 
You have a strong background in pastry, desserts and contemporary techniques.

• 
You are creative, detail-oriented and passionate about flavour, texture and presentation.

• 
You thrive in a professional kitchen where precision and consistency are essential.

• 
You are organised, take responsibility and enjoy working as part of a dedicated team.

• 
You are motivated by continuous learning, development and pushing culinary boundaries.

What we offer

• 
A key position in an ambitious Michelin-starred restaurant.

• 
The opportunity to influence and develop the pastry direction at Okê.

• 
Close collaboration with a passionate and highly skilled culinary team.

• 
A creative working environment with a strong focus on craftsmanship, quality and professional development.

• 
The opportunity to work at Ruths Hotel, situated in the beautiful surroundings of Gl. Skagen, Denmark.

How to apply

If you share our passion for exceptional gastronomy and would like to become part of Restaurant Okê, we would love to hear from you.

Please send your application and CV in English to job@ruths-hotel.dk, with the subject line Sous Chef – Restaurant Okê.

We look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Digitalization
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for one or more vacant Assistant Professorship (s) in Information Systems and Digitalization at the Department of Digitalization.

CBS is a globally recognized business school with a robust interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment. The Department of Digitalization is an engaged and diverse community of scholars exploring the interplay between technology and organizations, with impact-driven research and teaching at its core. Our main research areas include (but not exclusively):

1. Business intelligence and data science

2. Data studies

3. Digital ecosystem and sustainability

4. Digital government

5. IT management and enterprise architecture

6. Hybrid threats and defence tech

7. Digital transformation of work and society

We prioritize high-quality research and are committed to publishing in leading academic journals, with a particular focus on the AIS premier journal list (https://aisnet.org/research/seniorscholarsbasket/ ).

Teaching responsibilities of the department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching in Digitalization, please read more about our programmes: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/departments-and-centres/ department-of-digitalization/ degree-programmes

We are interested in candidates with a PhD in Information Systems and Digitalization, ideally with a strong technical background (e.g., MSc in Computer Science, Data Science, or related fields).

Candidates are expected to have a promising research pipeline and a commitment to contribute to advancing scholarship in the fields of information systems and digitalization.

We are particularly interested in candidates who can teach following subjects:

• 
Data science, Artificial Intelligence, and their mathematical and computational foundations (e.g., linear algebra, machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing)

• 
Cyber security

• 
Enterprise architecture

The assistant professorship is a tenure track position (6 years) with research and teaching obligations.

To fulfil the research requirements of the position, the applicant(s) chosen is expected to be physically present on a regular basis and actively participate in the teaching and research activities of the Department. The successful applicant is obliged to participate in the assistant professor program at CBS on teaching principles and methods in order to fulfil the pedagogical requirements made at the end of the term of employment as assistant professor.

Responsibilities 

• 
Teaching and associated examination in existing CBS programs, including Executive Education

• 
Individual and group based research meeting high international standards

• 
Promoting CBS’s academic reputation

• 
Initiating, fund raising and coordinating research projects

• 
Promoting the teaching and research capabilities of Copenhagen Business School and other relevant assignments at Copenhagen Business School

• 
Contributing to the administrative responsibilities of the department and to CBS-wide tasks

• 
Communicating findings to the public in general and to CBS’s stakeholders in particular

• 
Research, including responsibility for the academic development of the relevant discipline

• 
Responsibility for publishing, scientific communication and research-based teaching

• 
Active participation in the regular research activities, such as research seminars, workshops and conferences.

The assistant professor is expected to contribute to the development and application of the research of the department’s research areas and to maintain and strengthen CBS’s international research position. 

Qualification 

The applicant must hold a PhD or the equivalent. Emphasis is placed on the applicant’s research potential, which means that a researcher with a large research potential may be preferred to a researcher with a large research production. 

The applicant must have professional proficiency in English (written and spoken). 

Copenhagen Business School has a broad commitment to the excellence, distinctiveness and relevance of its teaching and research programmes. Candidates who wish to join us should demonstrate enthusiasm for working in an organisation of this type.

For further information please contact: Head of Department Andrea Carugati via e-mail ac.digi@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/digi.

Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organisation.

Application 

Application must be sent via the electronic recruitment system.

Application must include: 

• 
A statement of application.

• 
Proof of qualifications and a full CV.

• 
Documentation of relevant, significant, original research at an international level, including publications in the field’s internationally recognized journals and citations in the Social Science Citation Index and/or Google Scholar.

• 
A teaching portfolio documenting teaching qualifications and pedagogical development. The portfolio must include an overview of the applicants past teaching achievements and practice and its impact on the students, reflections on pedagogical competencies and core strengths, the educational competencies the applicant would like to develop, and the teaching opportunities they would like to pursue in the nearest future. External applicants can see the full description of the teaching portfolio here. Internal applicants must use the CBS Teaching Portfolio format. It is available at www.share.cbs.dk. Please make a pdf of each of the spreadsheets from part B of the portfolio.

• 
Information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation and international co-operation.

• 
A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 10 publications for review are allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.

• 
Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration.

Recruitment procedure 

The Recruitment Committee will shortlist minimum two applicants; when possible five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline.

The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.

jobs.occupation: Business Consultant, Regulatory Banking Services, Netcompany Banking Services
jobs.description:
Job Description

Would you like to work with financial regulation and compliance while contributing to the development of a growing regulatory services business at Netcompany Banking Services?

As a Business Consultant, you will work with compliance and risk management while supporting legal and governance matters for financial institutions. You will combine your regulatory expertise with an analytical and structured approach to help our customers navigate complex regulatory requirements and strengthen their compliance and risk frameworks.

We are currently expanding our regulatory services offering, where you will play an important role in delivering and further developing our services to financial institutions. Our services within the compliance and risk areas cover the regulatory process from monitoring legislation and assessing compliance risks to annual planning, data-supported compliance reviews and regulatory reporting.

We focus on the use of automation and new technologies to develop efficient and scalable regulatory services. Working closely with colleagues across data and technology, you will contribute to high-quality customer deliveries and the continued development of regulatory Services.

Netcompany Banking Services

We deliver various IT solutions and services to banks and savings institutions across Denmark and other Nordic countries. We provide a modern, cloud-based core banking platform serving more than 50 Nordic banks with over 2 million end customers. Our solutions encompass daily banking operations, mobile and internet banking, payments, investment management, risk management, compliance, and open banking.

Responsibilities

As a Business Consultant, you will support the Head of Regulatory Banking Services in delivering high-quality regulatory services to financial institutions. You will contribute to daily customer deliveries while helping to develop and standardise processes, control frameworks and reporting models.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• 
Prepare and maintain compliance risk assessments and annual compliance plans for financial clients.

•

A property manager can handle 600 tenants. That's the industry limit. Why? Because the work scales linearly: matching bank transactions to invoices, chasing late payments, answering tenant questions, coordinating repairs, preparing legal notices, renewing leases. With AI, that limit disappears. And both landlords and tenants get a better experience.

**About Rumli

**Eight years in property operations. ~1,000 customers across Denmark, the Netherlands, and Germany. We know this industry: the workflows, the pain points, the regulations.

Now we're making a big move: becoming a property manager. Tenant communication, bookkeeping, coordinating repairs. We handle it all. A landlord shouldn't chase late payments or find a plumber at 10 pm. We do it for them.

We're building an entirely new platform to power this. AI-native from day one. Profitable, real customers, expanding across the Nordics.

**Why this is interesting

**Property management is a great domain for a product engineer. Thousands of similar transactions, pattern-based decisions, templated documents. And 1,000 customers who will tell you exactly where it hurts. Years of domain knowledge, ready to turn into a product.

We ship with AI agents built into the workflow. Our codebase has custom skills to improve our workflow. AI writes a lot of the code; we review it. That means the slow part of building isn't writing code anymore. It's knowing what to build. That's what this role is about.

**The role

**You are autonomous and independent, working with the team to solve property managers' pains and make them as efficient as possible.

• Talk to customers and property managers. Find out what actually slows them down

• Decide what to build, then build it. Mockup, prototype, ship, measure, repeat

• Own features end-to-end. Database to API to UI

• Build AI into core product features

• Work directly with our co-founder on product direction

We need someone who looks at a messy problem and figures out what to build, and doesn't wait for a spec.

**Tech stack

**TypeScript everywhere. But does it even matter anymore?

• Frontend: Next.js, React, Shadcn, Tailwind CSS

• Backend: NestJS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM

• Infra: AWS Lambda, CDK, RDS, EventBridge, SQS

**What We're Looking For

**

• Product thinking. You understand what it takes to build a profitable product. You are not here just to handle tickets.

• Strong product mindset. Agents can code, but they need scoping and steering.

• You've shipped things people actually use, and you can show them.

• Comfortable talking to customers.

• Experience with coding agents.

• Work independently.

• Copenhagen-based (on-site).

Big plus: AWS, AI experience (prompt engineering, RAG, agents), fintech/proptech background, a side project you're proud of.

**Compensation & Benefits

**

• Compensation: 50–65K DKK, depending on experience and demonstrated competencies

• Equity: Employee warrants offering real ownership in the company

• Workspace: Centrally located Copenhagen office

• Perks: Daily lunch included

**Why Rumli?

**Real customers. Brand-new codebase. Small team where your decisions matter.

Pharma communication is slow for a good reason. Every claim needs a reference, every asset needs approval, and every market has its own rules. We think the software that wins in this industry treats those rules as part of the product rather than something to work around, and that is what we build.

Anthill builds the software pharmaceutical companies use to create, approve and run their digital communication. At some of the world's largest pharma companies, commercial and medical teams rely on our products to produce and distribute regulated content. We're around 70 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, with four products: Activator, Arcane, Amplify and Anthill Cloud. Our products are already delivering GenAI-powered capabilities to Enterprise customers around the world.

We're growing fast, and it's a good time to join. In our Copenhagen office, engineers, designers, product people and strategists all sit in the same room. We're 15+ nationalities, so English is the official and everyday language in the office and in the codebase.

We are hiring a software engineer into our backend chapter.

What you will actually work on

Anthill Cloud is the shared platform layer behind our products. It handles identity, tenancy, content and the services that belong across the suite rather than inside any one product. Most of the interesting backend work at Anthill over the next two years sits on that line: deciding what belongs to a product, what belongs to the platform, and how to move something from one to the other without breaking a client who is mid-campaign.

We run on AWS. Lambda, ECS, API Gateway, EventBridge, DynamoDB, RDS, S3 and CloudWatch, with Terraform as how infrastructure gets changed. The code is Node: TypeScript on NestJS for Anthill Cloud, and JavaScript in parts of the product backends.

Coding agents write a growing share of that code, which moves most of the engineering to the work around it: shaping the solution, running spikes before anyone commits to an approach, building the harness agents work inside, orchestrating the work, and judging what comes back. You still write the code yourself when that is the better way.

In your first year you will:

• Shape solutions before they are built: service boundaries, contracts and data models, written down as decision records in the repo that people and agents build from.

• Run spikes that answer a technical question with evidence before a mission commits to an approach, and throw the spike away once it has.

• Build the harness our agents work inside: the specs, agent instructions, tests and checks that keep generated code inside the architecture, and tighten it when something gets through.

• Orchestrate agent work on changes that span several services: split it so agents can do it well, and own how the pieces fit together.

• Build and run services on Anthill Cloud, serverless or containerised depending on what the workload actually needs.

• Turn product-level capability into shared services the rest of the suite can call, including the unglamorous part where you migrate the original caller.

• Build integrations into the systems our clients already run, including Veeva, DAM platforms and client identity providers. Pharma clients do not adopt tools that ignore their existing stack.

• Work on the data models behind content authoring, modular content and referencing. The domain has real structure to it and getting the model wrong is expensive.

• Run what you build. You will have production access, you will see your own service misbehave, and you will fix it.

The levels

We are hiring at mid or senior level and will fit the role to the person we meet. The kind of work is the same at both. What changes is scope. A mid owns features and the design inside them, and works well inside service boundaries and agent setups that someone else defined. A senior owns decisions that outlast the mission they were made in, and other engineers and agents build on them. Tell us where you think you sit, and we will tell you if we see it differently. You do not need to tick every box below. Some of this is learned here.

What we are looking for

• Backend development against cloud services, ideally AWS.

• JavaScript, TypeScript and Node you can write well yourself, without an agent.

• Hands-on work with databases, both SQL and NoSQL.

• Infrastructure as code. We use Terraform.

• CI/CD pipelines, and some appetite for the operational side of what you ship.

• API design for consumers you do not control, and the discipline that comes with not being able to change them at will.

• Solution design you have done yourself and lived with: service boundaries, contracts and data models, written clearly enough that an engineer or an agent can build from it, including the decisions you would now make differently.

• Spikes and prototypes that answered a question rather than became the product, and the discipline to throw them away.

• Experience with agent-driven development: daily work with coding agents such as Claude Code, building the context, instructions and checks they work inside, splitting work so they can do it well, reviewing what comes back to the standard you would hold a colleague to, and knowing when to stop and write it yourself.

• Working English. Danish is not required.

Useful, not required:

• NestJS and TypeORM, or another structured Node framework.

• Event-driven architecture, and experience with the failure modes rather than the diagrams.

• Python or another backend language alongside Node.

• Experience in a regulated industry: GxP, validated systems, ISO 27001, or anything where an auditor eventually reads your change log.

• Work on AI features in production, including retrieval and evaluation. We run on AWS Bedrock and have a dedicated AI chapter you would work alongside.

• Agent tooling you have built yourself: MCP servers, agent instructions shared across a team, or evaluations of what agents produce.

How we work

Engineers belong to a chapter and work in missions. The chapter is your professional home and where your craft is developed.

Missions are time boxed, cross functional teams pointed at one outcome. When a round of missions closes, people rotate and a new set forms. The rotation is the point. Over a couple of years you work with most of the engineering team and across most of the product surface, instead of spending three years in one squad on one corner of the codebase.

Product decisions run through HIVE, our gate model. Nothing gets built because someone senior liked the idea. Initiatives pass through evidence, solution framing and a funding decision before engineering starts, and they are not closed until the outcome is validated rather than when the code ships. As an engineer this means you get told why something is being built, and you are expected to argue if the reasoning is thin.

What is agreed gets written down in the repo, as docs and decision records that people and coding agents both work from. A growing share of the engineering is in that writing and in the review, rather than in typing the code.

We work trunk based on Anthill Cloud and review each other's code, including the code our agents write. We expect the person who merges something to be able to explain how it runs, and we hold the line on security and access because our clients audit us and we hold their data.

What we offer

• A permanent Danish employment contract, pension and health insurance.

• A salary set from our salary bands, the same way for everyone at the same level. Where you land in the range depends on your experience and skills, and on pay equity with colleagues at that level.

• Five days a week in our Copenhagen office, with two work from home days a month as the default. We are on site because most of what engineers learn from each other happens in conversation at someone's desk.

• Colleagues who have shipped software into pharma and know how demanding that audience is.

• Clients whose problems are specific and constrained, which is more interesting than it sounds.

• Occasional office dogs, who expect to be petted.

In the interview you use the tools you use at work, coding agents included. You will also write some code without one, review code an agent wrote and tell us what is wrong with it, and take a design problem from question to plan with us: how you would shape the service, what you would spike first, and how you would set agents up to build it.

Sebastian Søberg leads the backend chapter and would be your manager. He is also our Senior Solution Architect and the person you argue with about architecture, which we consider a feature. Questions about the role can go to him on LinkedIn.

You will help make the architectural decisions at the platform layer, not be handed the result of them.

Applying

If you can recognise yourself in just some of these requirements or skills and simply want to learn the rest, we would love to receive your application. We offer an open environment with freedom under responsibility, where you have the opportunity to grow professionally.

Apply through LinkedIn, or get in touch directly if you would rather have a conversation before a formal application. We read everything ourselves.

Your CV does not need a photo, your age or anything else that is not about your work.

If there is a repository, a component library, a test plan, a bug report you are proud of, a design document or a postmortem that tells us more than a cover letter would, send that too.
